title: The teenage couple supposedly kills the grandmother after she refuses to let her boyfriend stay
text:
A teenage couple accused of killing the girl’s grandmother and fleeing through Texas was arrested after allegedly cutting and dyeing her hair to evade the police. Tara King, 17, and her 18 -year -old boyfriend, Uriah Ureck, were captured in Laredo on Sunday and admitted to the Galveston County prison on Monday night.
The couple faces capital assassination and abuse of credit or debit cards in the death of Tammy King, 61, Tara’s grandmother. Tammy King was shot dead inside his Bacliff’s house on February 5 after his boyfriend requested a social assistance check, Ktrk reported .

Deputies of Galveston County Sheriff Office He discovered his body in the 4700 block of 15th Street, noting that the house had been looted and that weapons were missing in a safe of a room. A worried neighbor informed that no one had heard from Tammy since Tuesday before his body was discovered.
Tara King (left) and Uriah Ulrick (right) are accused of killing Tammy King after she did not allow the couple to spend the night together at her home (Galveston County Sheriff’s Office) Judicial records reveal that Tammy and Tara had discussed Tara Skinging School before murder. The researchers also found transactions of cash applications from Tammy’s account to Tara’s, which suggests financial motifs. During their time in the race, the couple allegedly tried to sell stolen weapons and looked for trips to Wyoming, Fox 26 Houston reported .
Police say they offered money to the acquaintances for their help, and Tara told a friend: “I will not be able to talk to my family after this.” The coroner confirmed that Tammy died of bullet wounds. After a one -day human hunt, the authorities tracked adolescents to Laredo, where they were arrested without incident.

The case has shocked the Bacliff community, with the neighbors who express disbelief for the brutal crime. Tara and Ureck remain in custody as the investigation continues, and prosecutors probably pursue severe sanctions given the position of capital murder.
